thread:
marta: Heads up — firewall default-deny rollout in eu-central-1 pushed at 11:02 UTC and new GPU onboarding jobs are failing to reach keystore + docker registry. Seeing lots of 403s in provisioning logs.
tom: Oof. Which rule blocked what? Any concrete log lines?
marta: pasted a snippet from provisioning-controller logs (trimmed):
```
2025-03-14T11:05:21Z WARN http: GET https://keystore.eu-central-1.internal/keys -> 403 Forbidden
2025-03-14T11:05:22Z ERROR imagepull: failed to pull image redwood/gpu-infer:1.2.4 from registry.internal -> dial tcp 10.2.4.17:443: i/o timeout
2025-03-14T11:05:23Z ERROR provision: node-init failed: network unreachable
```
devin: Looks like the new rule denied egress to our privatelink endpoints (keystore + registry). Firewall team scoped default-deny by endpoint cidr instead of service tags. That would block the privatelink ENIs.
sre-bot: alert: capacity-onboard-fail spike (rate=85/min) region:eu-central-1 severity: P1
marta: confirmed in AWS VPC flow logs: ACCEPT -> traffic to privatelink ENI dropped because SG was updated to only allow to 0.0.0.0/0 on port 443, but NACL had deny on the ENI subnet.
tom: Quick mitigation: can we add a temporary SG egress rule to allow traffic to the private endpoints CIDRs and open the NACL entries? Who can push that?
devin: I can do SG change now and add NACL allow for the subnet. Doing it via CLI: `aws ec2 authorize-security-group-egress --group-id sg-0a1b2c3d --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 10.0.0.0/16` and `aws ec2 replace-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id acl-0abcd --cidr-block 10.0.0.0/16 --rule-action allow --egress false --rule-number 100 --protocol -1`
ops-bot: runbook action: creating incident record infra-403-firewall-eu (assigned to @devin).
marta: Please also re-enable VPC Flow Logs for the affected VPCs if disabled during the change so audit data exists. Audit team requested flow logs for the time window.
audit-bot: note: flow logs for vpc-0aaa will be ingested. retention policy: 90d. Correlate with keystore rotation events.
tom: after SG + NACL patch, nodes started pulling images. Warm-pool warmup resumed but we lost ~12 nodes of warm capacity and autoscaler started provisioning which hit quota limits. We had to request temporary quota bump.
ops-bot: AWS quota increase submitted (req-12034) for eu-central-1 GPU vCPUs. Expected 45m.
devin: We're seeing extra NAT egress because registry pulls fell back to a public mirror during outage — projected additional cost ~ $720/day if sustained. Not huge but worth tracking.
marta: good to know. For now set eviction pause for 20m to avoid further churn while warm pool rebuilds. Patch HPA: `kubectl patch hpa gpu-warmpool -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":6}}'`
tom: done. HPA patched and annotated with incident id. Batch queues leveling.
sre-bot: capacity onboarding error rate back to baseline. Monitoring: `avg:infra.provision.fail_rate{region:eu-central-1}` down from 0.9 to 0.02 in 18m.
marta: follow-ups: 1) Update firewall rollout checklist to include privatelink ENI cidr whitelist and NACL test, 2) add preflight check that calls keystore + registry via the new rules from a canary subnet, 3) add billing alert on unexpected NAT egress > $300/day.
devin: I'll own preflight and the canary job. Will open a PR for checklist and add tests to ci/integration.
audit-bot: incident closed: infra-403-firewall-eu (severity: S2). artifacts: flowlogs, provisioning logs, acl diff uploaded to https://wiki.redwood.ai/incidents/infra-403-firewall-eu-1767778888
marta: thanks all. closing once PRs merge and quota bump comes through. :thumbsup:
